lessons.title: Conducting a Topographic Survey
lessons.body:
A topographic survey shows the shape and slope of your land. You need it to design a pond that fills and drains by gravity, avoiding pumps. Start by walking the site at the driest time of year. Use a dumpy level, tripod, and levelling staff. If you don't have these, a water-filled hose and two clear plastic pipes work as a water level. For a 20m x 30m pond, take readings every 5 metres along grid lines. Record elevations in a notebook.

Set up your level where you can see the whole area. Take a backsight on a known point (like a concrete benchmark or a large rock). Then take foresights at each grid point. Subtract foresight from backsight to get the height difference. If the difference is positive, the ground is lower; negative, higher. Write these numbers down. For example, if backsight is 1.5m and foresight is 2.0m, the ground is 0.5m lower than your level.

After surveying, draw a contour map. Contours are lines connecting points of equal elevation. Use a 0.25m contour interval for flat land, 0.5m for hilly. This map shows where water will flow. You want a slope of 1-2% for a pond bottom, so water moves to the drain. If the slope is more than 5%, you'll need to cut and fill more soil, which costs money.

In Africa, many sites are uneven. If you find a natural depression, use it. Otherwise, plan to move soil from the high side to the low side. Calculate the volume: area x average depth difference. For a 600mÂ² pond with 0.5m average difference, you need to move 300mÂ³ of soil. That's about 30 trips with a 10mÂ³ tipper truck. Always mark your survey points with wooden pegs and flagging tape so you don't lose them.

Finally, check for underground rocks or old tree stumps. A simple probe (a metal rod) pushed into the ground can find them. If you hit rock, you may need to blast or relocate. A good survey saves you from building a pond that won't drain or hold water.

lessons.title: Soil Testing for Pond Suitability
lessons.body:
The best soil for a fish pond has at least 20% clay. Clay holds water; sand and gravel leak. To test, dig a hole 50cm deep. Take a handful of soil from the bottom. Squeeze it in your fist. If it forms a ribbon that hangs together for 5cm or more, it's good clay. If it crumbles, it's too sandy. Do this test in at least five spots across the site.

Next, do a jar test. Fill a clear 1-litre jar one-third with soil, add water to the top, and shake hard for 3 minutes. Let it settle for 24 hours. Sand settles first, then silt, then clay. Measure each layer with a ruler. If clay is less than 20% of the total, you need to import clay or use a plastic liner. For a 20m x 30m pond, you'd need about 40 tonnes of clay to mix into the top 30cm.

Check for soil pH. Use a cheap pH test kit from an agro-vet shop. Ideal pH is 6.5 to 8.5. If below 6.0, add agricultural lime at 2 tonnes per hectare. If above 9.0, add gypsum. Also test for salinity: if you're near the coast, use an EC meter. Fish like tilapia tolerate up to 2,000 ÂµS/cm, but catfish prefer below 1,000 ÂµS/cm.

In many parts of Africa, termites and earthworms indicate good soil. If you see many termite mounds, the soil is often clay-rich. Avoid black cotton soil that cracks when dryâit leaks when wet. Also avoid soils with high organic matter (like peat) because they decompose and cause oxygen problems.

If your soil fails, don't give up. You can compact it with a sheepsfoot roller, add bentonite clay (10kg per mÂ²), or line the pond with HDPE geomembrane (0.5mm thick). The liner costs about $3 per mÂ², so for a 600mÂ² pond, that's $1,800. Testing first saves you from spending that money unnecessarily.

lessons.title: Water Source Evaluation and Testing
lessons.body:
You need a reliable water source that provides at least 5% of your pond volume daily to replace evaporation and seepage. For a 600mÂ³ pond, that's 30,000 litres per day. Measure your source: stream flow, borehole yield, or rainwater. For a stream, use a bucket and stopwatch. If a 20-litre bucket fills in 10 seconds, flow is 2 litres per second, or 172,800 litres per dayâmore than enough.

Test water quality before you commit. Use a test kit for dissolved oxygen (DO), pH, temperature, and ammonia. DO should be above 5 mg/L. If below 3 mg/L, fish will gasp at the surface. pH should be 6.5-8.5. Ammonia should be below 0.5 mg/L. In Africa, many boreholes have high iron or sulphur. If water smells like rotten eggs, it has hydrogen sulphideâtoxic to fish. Aerate it by splashing into a storage tank before use.

Check for pesticides and herbicides if you're near farmland. These kill fish. A simple bioassay: put 10 small tilapia in a bucket of source water. If more than 2 die in 24 hours, the water is unsafe. Also test for heavy metals if near mining areasâuse a lab test, which costs about $50.

Rainwater is the cheapest source. A roof of 100mÂ² in a region with 800mm annual rainfall collects 80,000 litres per year. That's 219 litres per dayâenough for a small pond. But you need storage. A 10,000-litre tank costs $500. For groundwater, drill a borehole (cost $3,000-$8,000) and test yield with a pump test. You want at least 1 litre per second.

Always have a backup source. If your stream dries up, you need a borehole or stored water. In dry season, many African ponds fail because the source disappears. Plan for the worst month, not the best.

lessons.title: Assessing Drainage and Flood Risks
lessons.body:
A pond must drain completely for harvest and maintenance. You need a low point with a drain pipe. If your site is flat, create a 1% slope toward the drain. For a 30m long pond, that's a 30cm drop from inlet to outlet. Use a water level to check. If the land slopes the wrong way, you'll need to cut a channel or install a pumpâexpensive.

Flood risk is critical. In Africa, many ponds are lost to seasonal floods. Check the high-water mark: look for debris lines on trees, silt deposits, or ask elders. If your site floods more than once every 5 years, don't build there. Alternatively, build a dyke (embankment) at least 1m above the highest flood level. For a 600mÂ² pond, a 1m high dyke with 2:1 side slopes needs about 200mÂ³ of soil.

Assess drainage away from the pond. You don't want overflow to erode your dyke or flood downstream neighbours. Dig a diversion channel 1m deep and 1m wide around the uphill side. This channel should slope at 0.5% to carry water away. If the channel is 50m long, it drops 25cm. Use a line level and string to check.

In heavy rain, your pond may overflow. Install a spillwayâa concrete or grassed channel that carries excess water safely. Size it for a 1-in-10-year storm. For a 1-hectare catchment, that's about 0.5mÂ³ per second. A spillway 2m wide and 0.3m deep can handle that. Never let water flow over the dyke; it will breach.

Also check groundwater. If the water table is within 0.5m of the surface in dry season, you may not need a liner. But if it's high in wet season, the pond may float if emptied. In that case, keep the pond full or install a pressure relief valve. Simple test: dig a hole 1m deep. If it fills with water within 24 hours, the water table is high.

lessons.title: Marking Pond Boundaries and Levels
lessons.body:
Once you've chosen the pond location, mark it clearly. Use wooden pegs (30cm long) and bright flagging tape. For a rectangular pond, drive pegs at all four corners. For irregular shapes, use a rope to outline the edge. Check square corners with the 3-4-5 method: measure 3m along one side, 4m along the other, and the diagonal should be 5m. Adjust until it is.

Mark the pond bottom level. The bottom should be flat or slope 1% toward the drain. Use a dumpy level or water level to set grade stakes. Drive a stake at the outlet (lowest point) and mark the desired bottom elevation. Then drive stakes every 5m along the pond length. Use a string line between stakes to show the bottom grade. For a 30m pond with 1% slope, the inlet end is 30cm higher than the outlet.

Mark the top of the dyke. The dyke should be 0.5m above the water level. For a 1.5m deep pond, the dyke top is 2.0m above the bottom. Use a level to mark this on corner pegs. Also mark the inside and outside toes of the dyke. The inside toe is where the dyke meets the pond bottom; the outside toe is where it meets the original ground. For a 1m high dyke with 2:1 slopes, the base is 1m + 2*(1m) = 3m wide on each side? Actually, for a 1m high dyke, top width 1m, side slopes 2:1, the base width = 1m + 2*2*1m = 5m. Mark these with pegs.

Use a permanent marker: concrete monuments or steel pipes at corners. Write the elevation on them. In Africa, cattle and people may knock over wooden pegs. So after marking, take GPS coordinates of each corner. Record them in a notebook. If pegs are lost, you can re-establish them with GPS.

Finally, mark the inlet and outlet. The inlet should be at the highest point, with a pipe or channel. The outlet (drain) at the lowest point, with a monk or standpipe. Mark these with different coloured tape. Check that water will flow by gravity from inlet to outlet. If not, adjust your levels before digging.

lessons.title: Using GPS and Drones for Site Mapping
lessons.body:
A handheld GPS (like Garmin eTrex) costs about $100 and is accurate to 3-5 metres. Walk the pond boundary and mark waypoints at each corner. Record the coordinates (latitude, longitude, elevation). Download them to a computer using free software like QGIS. This gives you a map with area and perimeter. For a 20m x 30m pond, you should get 600mÂ². If your GPS says 550mÂ², check your walking line.

For better accuracy, use a GPS with external antenna or a smartphone app like GPS Fields Area Measure. These can be accurate to 1-2 metres. Mark the four corners, then use the app to calculate area. Also mark the water source, inlet, outlet, and any obstacles (trees, rocks). Take photos with geotags.

Drones are becoming affordable. A basic drone like the DJI Mini 2 costs $400. Fly at 50m height with 70% overlap between photos. Use free software like OpenDroneMap to stitch images into an orthomosaic map. This map shows every detail: slopes, vegetation, wet spots. You can measure distances and elevations. For a 1-hectare site, a drone flight takes 10 minutes and processes in 1 hour.

In Africa, drone rules vary. In Kenya, you need a permit from the Kenya Civil Aviation Authority. In Nigeria, register with NCAA. Always fly in open areas, away from airports and people. If you can't afford a drone, hire a surveyor with one. A drone survey for a small pond costs $200-$500, but it saves days of manual surveying.

Use GPS and drone data to plan your pond. Import the map into QGIS, draw the pond shape, and calculate cut and fill volumes. For example, if the drone map shows a 0.5m elevation difference across the site, you know you need to move 300mÂ³ of soil. Also use the map to plan drainage channels and access roads. Share the map with your digger operatorâthey can see exactly where to dig. This reduces errors and saves fuel.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of a topographic survey for a fish pond?
options: B) To determine the slope and shape of the land
quiz.explanation: A topographic survey shows elevation changes, which are essential for designing a pond that drains by gravity.

quiz.q: Which tool can be used as a simple water level for surveying?
options: B) A clear plastic hose filled with water
quiz.explanation: A water-filled hose acts as a water level because water seeks its own level, allowing you to compare elevations.

quiz.q: What is the recommended contour interval for flat land in a topographic survey?
quiz.explanation: For flat land, a smaller contour interval like 0.25m gives more detail for pond design.

quiz.q: If a backsight reading is 1.5m and a foresight is 2.0m, what is the height difference?
quiz.explanation: Subtract foresight from backsight: 1.5 - 2.0 = -0.5, meaning the ground is 0.5m lower than the level.

quiz.q: What is the ideal slope for a pond bottom to allow drainage?
quiz.explanation: A 1-2% slope allows water to flow to the drain without causing erosion.

quiz.q: How many cubic metres of soil must be moved if a 600mÂ² pond has an average depth difference of 0.5m?
quiz.explanation: Volume = area x depth difference = 600mÂ² x 0.5m = 300mÂ³.

quiz.q: What minimum percentage of clay is ideal for a fish pond soil?
quiz.explanation: At least 20% clay is needed to hold water and prevent seepage.

quiz.q: In a jar test, which soil layer settles first?
quiz.explanation: Sand particles are largest and settle first, followed by silt, then clay.

quiz.q: What is the ideal pH range for pond water?
quiz.explanation: Most fish species thrive in water with pH between 6.5 and 8.5.

quiz.q: If soil pH is below 6.0, what should you add?
quiz.explanation: Agricultural lime raises pH and is commonly used to correct acidic soils.

quiz.q: What does a ribbon test of 5cm or more indicate?
quiz.explanation: A long ribbon indicates good clay content, which is suitable for pond lining.

quiz.q: Which soil type should be avoided for pond construction?
quiz.explanation: Black cotton soil cracks when dry and leaks when wet, making it unsuitable for ponds.

quiz.q: How much water does a 600mÂ³ pond need daily to replace losses?
quiz.explanation: 5% of 600mÂ³ is 30mÂ³, which equals 30,000 litres per day.

quiz.q: What is the minimum dissolved oxygen level for healthy fish?
quiz.explanation: Dissolved oxygen should be above 5 mg/L; below 3 mg/L fish suffer.

quiz.q: If water smells like rotten eggs, which gas is present?
quiz.explanation: Hydrogen sulphide gives a rotten egg smell and is toxic to fish.

quiz.q: What is a simple bioassay to test water safety for fish?
options: A) Add salt and see if it dissolves
B) Put 10 small tilapia in a bucket of source water for 24 hours
C) Measure pH with a meter
quiz.explanation: If more than 2 fish die in 24 hours, the water contains toxins.

quiz.q: How much water can a 100mÂ² roof collect in a region with 800mm annual rainfall?
quiz.explanation: 100mÂ² x 0.8m = 80mÂ³ = 80,000 litres per year.

quiz.q: What is the minimum recommended slope for a drainage channel?
quiz.explanation: A 0.5% slope allows water to flow without causing erosion.

quiz.q: How high should a dyke be built above the highest flood level?
quiz.explanation: A 1m freeboard above flood level protects the pond from overtopping.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a spillway?
options: A) To drain the pond completely
B) To carry excess water safely during heavy rain
quiz.explanation: A spillway prevents dyke failure by diverting overflow.

quiz.q: What does the 3-4-5 method check?
quiz.explanation: The 3-4-5 triangle ensures corners are exactly 90 degrees.

quiz.q: For a 30m long pond with 1% slope, what is the elevation difference between inlet and outlet?
quiz.explanation: 1% of 30m is 0.3m, or 30cm.

quiz.q: What is the base width of a 1m high dyke with 1m top width and 2:1 side slopes?
quiz.explanation: Base width = top width + 2 x (side slope x height) = 1 + 2 x (2 x 1) = 5m.

quiz.q: Why should you take GPS coordinates of pond corners?
options: B) To re-establish boundaries if pegs are lost
D) To calculate fish stocking density
quiz.explanation: GPS coordinates allow you to find corners even if physical markers are destroyed.

quiz.q: What is the typical accuracy of a basic handheld GPS?
quiz.explanation: Handheld GPS units are accurate to about 3-5 metres under normal conditions.

quiz.q: What is a key advantage of using a drone for site mapping?
options: B) It provides high-resolution maps quickly
D) It replaces the need for a surveyor
quiz.explanation: Drones can capture detailed aerial images that are processed into accurate maps in a short time.

quiz.q: In which African country would you need a permit from the Kenya Civil Aviation Authority to fly a drone?
quiz.explanation: Kenya requires drone operators to obtain a permit from the KCAA.

quiz.q: What free software can stitch drone images into a map?
quiz.explanation: OpenDroneMap is a free, open-source tool for processing drone imagery.

quiz.q: What is the main benefit of using GPS and drone data for pond planning?
options: B) It helps calculate cut and fill volumes accurately
D) It replaces the need for soil testing
quiz.explanation: Accurate elevation data from GPS and drones allows precise volume calculations for earthworks.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a sign of a high water table?
options: A) A hole dug 1m deep fills with water within 24 hours
B) The soil is very dry
quiz.explanation: If a 1m deep hole fills with water within a day, the water table is high.
